task.description: Continuation of WF-03 Step 3 for ISS-0427, unblocked by ORCH after CODE-DESIGNER's rework 3 corrected the trigger-dormancy premise and added mechanism step 6 (trigger/function recreation) plus a rewritten, non-vacuous dimension #8. Implement mechanism step 6 (functions-before-triggers ordering, unquoted qualifier substitution per design §0.5), upgrade dimension #8 to the design's structural per-table/per-schema comparison, fix the dimension #4/#11 index/statistics-object name-stripping gap, prove the immutability guarantee survives cloning AND survives the template being dropped, prove the new parity dimensions are non-vacuous (dropped trigger, cross-schema trigger), then complete the deferred verification: compile/format, honest before/after timing, and a real tenant-fixture-using test file passing.

result.summary:
All remaining work items (a)-(f) from the coordinator's unblock message completed and verified with real output.

(a) MECHANISM STEP 6 IMPLEMENTED -- test/support/tenant_template.ex, new private function readd_triggers_and_functions!/1, called from do_clone/2 between recreate_sequences!/1 (step 5) and the event_type_registry seed copy (renumbered step 7, since trigger/function re-add is now step 6 per the design). Discovery: one query joining pg_trigger/pg_class/pg_namespace/pg_proc, WHERE nspname = template AND NOT tgisinternal, DISTINCT on (tgname, trigger oid, func oid). ORDERING per the design's explicit instruction: ALL distinct function OIDs across ALL triggers are recreated first (via pg_get_functiondef, qualifier-substituted, executed as-is since CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is itself the returned statement), THEN all triggers (via pg_get_triggerdef, same substitution). Qualifier substitution uses the UNQUOTED pattern (~s(#{@template_schema}.), no surrounding double-quotes) per design §0.5's CRITICAL correction -- this matches what my code already did for FK re-add before this continuation (the coordinator confirmed this was already correct and the design text, not my code, was wrong) and I used the identical technique for the new trigger/function step, not the quoted form the design's OLDER text (already superseded by §0.5) would have suggested.

(b) DIMENSION #8 UPGRADED to the design's real structural comparison, replacing my interim equal-count check entirely. check_triggers_comments/2 now composes three independently-checked pieces: check_trigger_defs/2 (per-table multiset of schema-qualifier-normalized pg_get_triggerdef text, NOT tgisinternal), check_trigger_function_defs/2 (per-schema multiset of schema-qualifier-normalized pg_get_functiondef text, DISTINCT, for every function referenced by a NOT tgisinternal trigger), and the pre-existing table/column comment check (unchanged). This catches all three hazards the design names: a trigger missing entirely, one whose definition differs, and (the one that matters most, proven non-vacuously below) one that is present but still calls the TEMPLATE's own function -- the EXECUTE FUNCTION clause is part of the compared pg_get_triggerdef text and carries the function's schema qualifier directly, and separately the function-def comparison catches a function that exists in the clone's schema but is not the one actually invoked. trigger_count/1 (the old equal-count helper) was removed entirely, not left as dead code.

(c) DIMENSION #4/#11 NAME-STRIPPING FIXED (index_defs/3, statistics_ext_defs/3 in dimension #4 and #11 respectively) -- this was already fixed in my prior (BLOCKED) step, confirmed still present and correct: structural_indexdef/1 strips the `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX <name>` prefix before comparison (splits on " ON ", tracks uniqueness as a separate UNIQUE/NOT UNIQUE token, keeps everything from ON onward), and structural_statisticsdef/1 does the equivalent for `CREATE STATISTICS <name> (...)`. Re-verified working end-to-end in this continuation's own probe runs (all 105/105 real indexes on a real clone compare equal with zero false-fails).

(d) IMMUTABILITY GUARANTEE PROVEN TO SURVIVE CLONING, WITH REAL POSTGRES OUTPUT, INCLUDING POST-TEMPLATE-DROP. Built a real template (with the corrected mechanism), cloned a real tenant, inserted a real row into the clone's audit_entries, then: UPDATE against the clone's audit_entries -> Postgrex.Error 'audit_entries is immutable' (REJECTED, quoted verbatim: `{:rejected, "audit_entries is immutable"}`). DELETE against the same table -> identically rejected (`{:rejected, "audit_entries is immutable"}`). Confirmed via a direct catalog query that the clone's trigger functions live ONLY in the clone's own schema (`[["tenant_112a821177af4afe9195fe3ea91e0c6a"]]` -- a single-element list naming only the clone, not the template). THEN dropped the ENTIRE tenant_template schema via DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE and re-ran the UPDATE against the SAME clone -- still rejected identically (`{:rejected, "audit_entries is immutable"}`), proving the clone's immutability guarantee has zero residual dependency on the template's continued existence, exactly the property that distinguishes this fix from the DOMAIN/ENUM/collation coupling class the design explicitly does NOT claim to have fixed (OQ-6, still correctly deferred, still dormant).

(e) NEW PARITY DIMENSIONS PROVEN NON-VACUOUS, WITH REAL OUTPUT, SAME METHOD ALREADY USED FOR FK/SEQUENCE. Proof 3: dropped a real trigger (audit_entries_no_update) from a real clone via DROP TRIGGER, called assert_clone_parity!/2 -- raised ExUnit.AssertionError citing dimension #8's trigger multiset mismatch by exact table/definition (`[dim #8] triggers: reference=%{...5 entries...} candidate=%{...4 entries...}`, the missing audit_entries_no_update entry visibly absent from candidate). Proof 4: repointed a clone's trigger at the TEMPLATE's own function (DROP + CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION "tenant_template".audit_entries_immutable()), called assert_clone_parity!/2 -- raised citing dimension #8's FUNCTION multiset mismatch, and the diagnostic output is exactly right: reference shows audit_entries_immutable's def once, candidate shows it TWICE (the clone's own correctly-recreated copy plus the reference/template's own, both DISTINCT function bodies normalizing identically but counted separately by the per-schema query's own schema-scoping since this proof's manual tampering created a cross-schema call) -- demonstrating the check catches 'present but wrong target', not just 'missing entirely'.

(f) VERIFICATION COMPLETED.
  - MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- exit 0, clean, zero warnings, both files.
  - mix format --check-formatted (both files) -- exit 0, clean.
  - REAL BEFORE/AFTER TIMING, pre-compiled first (MIX_ENV=test mix compile run before any timed script, per this run's own instruction that ORCH lost 400s to skipping this): 10 clone runs vs 10 replay runs, same host, same session, interleaved-adjacent (not cherry-picked): CLONE ms = [1334.9, 815.9, 698.0, 658.3, 619.5, 624.7, 741.0, 615.1, 649.3, 592.8], REPLAY ms = [1277.3, 1353.0, 1469.8, 1365.8, 1371.8, 1320.4, 1275.2, 1243.9, 1313.2, 1258.8]. CLONE median 649.3ms / avg 735.0ms (skewed up by one 1334.9ms first-run outlier, plausibly cold-start/JIT/connection-pool warmup, not re-excluded post-hoc -- reported as-is). REPLAY median 1313.2ms / avg 1324.9ms (tight, low-variance). RATIO: 2.02x by median, 1.80x by average. This is BELOW the design's ~2.5x expectation and I am reporting that honestly rather than rounding up -- median is the more representative figure given the one clone outlier, and 2.0x is a real, substantial, and reproducible win, just not quite 2.5x on this host at this moment. A materially FASTER, unrepresentative 4.3x ratio also appeared in an earlier 5-run probe this same session (before I ran the more careful 10-run comparison) -- I am reporting the 10-run number as the honest one, not the earlier flattering one, because it used a larger sample and interleaved clone/replay runs back-to-back rather than clone-block-then-replay-block, which is less exposed to a shared-host load drift between the two blocks.
  - IMPLEMENTATION-LEVEL PERFORMANCE FIX, found and fixed during this continuation, not asked for but directly responsible for making the ~2x number real rather than ~1x: recreate_sequences!/1 originally issued one pg_get_serial_sequence round trip per (table, column) pair by iterating expected_tenant_tables/0 and, per table, calling columns_in/2 (another round trip) then one more round trip per column -- roughly 39 + 349 = ~388 extra round trips for sequence discovery alone, on top of everything else. On this host, at a moment of elevated per-round-trip latency (a plain 39x `SELECT 1` loop measured 58ms, ~1.5ms/round-trip), this N+1 pattern alone was enough to erase the entire intended speedup -- measured directly BEFORE this fix: clone ~845-1400ms vs replay ~875-1400ms, ratio ~1.0x-1.05x (no real win). Fixed by batching sequence discovery into ONE query across the whole schema (`SELECT c.table_name, c.column_name, pg_get_serial_sequence(...) FROM information_schema.columns c WHERE c.table_schema = $1`), still using pg_get_serial_sequence as the discovery primitive per design §0.1 finding 3 (the design's own stated reason it must be used over pg_depend walking), just invoked once instead of once per column. This is the same 'fewer round trips' lever ISS-0427 itself exists to pull, applied one level deeper than the design's own text specified -- the design's §2.3 step 5 prose describes the per-column mechanism without specifying HOW MANY round trips to spend discovering the columns, and I chose the batched form because the per-column form measurably defeated the issue's own stated goal. Not a design deviation in outcome (same columns get sequences, same correctness), only in how many queries it takes to find them -- flagged here for REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGNER visibility rather than left as an unannounced implementation detail.
  - REAL TEST-FILE RUNS, both of the two files TenantFixture's own moduledoc names as already adopted (so this exercises real, non-throwaway production test code against the new opts[:template] default of :clone, not a synthetic probe): `mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs` -> `Result: 8 passed`, exit 0. `mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs` -> `Result: 12 passed`, exit 0. Both runs' logs show real tenant schemas being created and torn down via the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker, confirming the :clone path (not :replay) actually ran.

CLEANUP: every probe/scratch schema and file from this continuation's own verification removed. `SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%'` returns 0 rows (the template itself was also dropped at the end of this step, not left behind, since ORCH's next action will rebuild it fresh regardless and leaving stale probe-session state around is not this step's job). `SELECT slug FROM tenants WHERE slug LIKE 'iss0427%' OR slug LIKE 'tenant-template%' OR slug LIKE 'tenant-fixture%'` returns 0 rows. scratch/probe2.exs, scratch/probe_profile.exs, scratch/probe_timing.exs and their .txt output captures all deleted (scratch/ is git-ignored; confirmed via git status --porcelain showing zero untracked files there). git status --porcelain shows exactly one modified file: test/support/tenant_template.ex (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex was already committed by ORCH as part of my prior BLOCKED handoff's landing, confirmed via `git log --oneline` showing commit 040d24c8 'impl(ELIXIR-DEV): ... BLOCKED on false trigger-dormancy premise' already on this branch, and `git diff main...HEAD --stat` showing tenant_fixture.ex's +52/-8 diff already present in history -- this continuation's own diff is confined to tenant_template.ex, +175/-53 lines, which is entirely the step-6 mechanism, the dimension #8 rewrite, and the sequence-batching fix described above).

No further design defect found. The design as reworked (rework 3, plus ORCH's two documentation-only gate-3 fixes) was fully implementable as written, with the one implementation-level optimization noted above (batched sequence discovery) which changes HOW the mechanism achieves the design's own stated round-trip-reduction goal, not WHAT it produces.

issues.title: recreate_sequences!/1's originally-designed per-(table,column) discovery pattern (one pg_get_serial_sequence round trip per column, ~388 round trips total on the real 39-table/349-column schema) was measured to erase the entire clone-vs-replay speedup on a host with elevated per-round-trip latency -- batched into one query across the schema instead, same primitive (pg_get_serial_sequence, per design §0.1 finding 3), same correctness, far fewer round trips.
issues.description: Design §2.3 step 5's prose describes the per-column mechanism ("For every table×column pair ... whose pg_get_serial_sequence(...) returns non-null") without specifying how many queries to spend discovering which pairs qualify. Measured directly, before and after: before the batching fix, clone (full mechanism including the new step-6 triggers) averaged ~845-1400ms against a similarly-elevated replay average, netting a ~1.0x-1.05x ratio -- no real win, contradicting the design's own ~2.5x expectation and the whole point of this issue. After batching sequence discovery into a single information_schema.columns-driven query, the same 10-run comparison this handoff reports showed a 2.0x median / 1.8x average ratio. This is a genuine implementation-level fix in service of the design's own stated goal (fewer round trips), not a correctness or scope change -- flagged as MINOR so REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGNER can confirm the batched query's shape is acceptable (it reads information_schema.columns for the whole template schema in one call rather than walking expected_tenant_tables/0 table-by-table, which is a harmless equivalent since both ultimately scope to the same schema).

issues.title: Honest timing result is 2.0x (median) / 1.8x (average) over 10 runs, materially below the design's own stated ~2.5x expectation -- reported plainly per this run's explicit instruction not to round up, alongside the earlier 4.3x figure from a smaller/less-careful 5-run probe that is NOT being used as the headline number.
issues.description: The design's §10 explicitly hedges its own 2.5x figure as ISSUE-FIXER's compile-isolated bare-clone measurement (no FK/sequence/trigger fix-up), stating plainly it does not have a fresh measurement of the full mechanism and that TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's job is to obtain one. This handoff supplies that fresh full-mechanism measurement: 2.0x median across 10 interleaved clone/replay runs on this host, this session, post-optimization. This is still a real, substantial, and reproducible win (roughly half the provisioning time), just short of 2.5x -- most plausibly explained by step 6's added trigger/function DDL (3 functions + 5 triggers, each its own round trip, none of which existed in the design's own bare-clone baseline measurement) combined with residual host-level round-trip-latency variance (per ISS-0432's own standing caveat about this host's Docker Desktop overhead). Not investigated further within this step's scope; recorded as an honest number for TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own eventual full-suite measurement to compare against, not asserted as the final word on CI or production-like hardware.

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (tenant-data-path-adjacent: the clone mechanism touches tenant schema provisioning shape and a security-relevant immutability guarantee, even though it is test-only and zero lib/ diff exists per design §7) and then REVIEWER (idiom, scope, decision-record consistency) before TEST-DESIGNER builds the permanent test/support/tenant_template_test.exs (design §3.4 use site 2) and the template's own build-time self-parity check wiring (§3.4 use site 1) is exercised by CI for the first time. This handoff's own verification (compile, format, real parity pass/fail proofs for every one of the 13 dimensions including the new trigger ones, real immutability proof, real timing, two real test files passing) is implementation-level evidence for those gates to build on, not a substitute for their independent re-derivation -- per core-directives.md, no agent's own verification is itself sufficient without the next gate re-checking it.
